title: Free AI Plans in India: Jio Gemini, ChatGPT Go and Airtel Compared
excerpt: Jio's free Google AI Pro is still open, Airtel's Perplexity Pro has closed and ChatGPT Go years renew soon. Terms, prices and privacy settings checked.
content:
As of 14 October 2026, only one of India's big free AI deals is still easy to claim: Jio's 18-month Google AI Pro offer for customers on a ₹349-or-higher 5G plan. Airtel's free Perplexity Pro closed to new claims on 16 January 2026, and the first free ChatGPT Go years, which started in November 2025, come up for renewal from next month. This guide checks each offer against the operators' and vendors' own pages, explains what you get and what you give up, and helps you work out what to keep paying for once the free period ends.

Key takeaways

  • Jio + Google AI Pro is the one big telecom offer still running. It gives 18 months of Google AI Pro, which Jio values at ₹35,100, to users aged 18 and over on an active 5G plan of ₹349 or more.
  • Airtel + Perplexity Pro stopped taking new claims on 16 January 2026. People who claimed it keep their 12 months, but Perplexity asks them to keep a valid payment method on file.
  • ChatGPT Go normally costs ₹399 a month in India. OpenAI made it free for a year for users who signed up in a promotion that began on 4 November 2025.
  • Free never means private by default. Google says Gemini chats can train its models and be read by human reviewers unless you change a setting.

Why the free AI plans arrived in India at once

Within roughly four months, between July and November 2025, India's two largest telecom operators and OpenAI each started giving away a paid AI subscription. Airtel moved first: on 17 July 2025 it announced that all of its roughly 360 million mobile, Wi-Fi and DTH customers could claim a year of Perplexity Pro free, according to Bharti Airtel's press release. The release valued that year at ₹17,000 (about $200).

OpenAI launched ChatGPT Go, a cheaper tier made for India, in August 2025 at ₹399 a month, about $4.60, TechCrunch reported. In late October it said Indian users who signed up during a limited promotion starting 4 November would get Go free for a year. TechCrunch noted that Sam Altman had called India OpenAI's second-largest market. Reliance and Google followed on 30 October 2025 with 18 months of Google's AI Pro plan for Jio users, Business Today reported.

The reasoning is the same in every case. India has more than 700 million smartphone users, but few of them pay for apps: TechCrunch cited Appfigures data showing ChatGPT took only $3.6 million in in-app purchases in India in the 90 days before August 2025, despite 29 million downloads. A free year gets an AI assistant into the daily routine, and a share of those people may later pay, or stay with the telecom operator that gave it to them.

Jio's Google AI Pro offer: what you get and the conditions

Jio's own page, published on 12 November 2025, sets out the current terms. Users aged over 18, on prepaid or postpaid, qualify if they have an active Jio 5G plan of ₹349 or more. They get 18 months of Google AI Pro, which Jio values at ₹35,100, according to Jio. The bundle includes:

  • Gemini 3 Pro in the Gemini app, plus Deep Research and NotebookLM
  • 5 TB of Google One storage shared across Drive, Photos and Gmail
  • Google's creative tools (Veo for video, Flow, Nano Banana for images, and Whisk), with up to 1,000 AI credits a month

To claim it, open the MyJio app, tap the Google Gemini offer banner on the home screen and sign in with your Google account. At launch the offer was limited to 18–25-year-olds on Unlimited 5G plans, and launch coverage listed 2 TB of storage. Jio has since opened it to all adults and its page now lists 5 TB. Business Today also reported that the benefit only continues while you stay on an Unlimited 5G plan, and that people already paying for Gemini Pro could move to the Jio-powered plan once their paid term ran out.

Jio's business page for postpaid corporate (COCP) plans, the plans an employer buys for staff, adds two useful details. You can claim the offer only once per mobile number, and once the 18 months are over there is "no payment or auto-renewal", according to Jio. In plain terms, the benefit ends and nothing is charged unless you decide to buy a plan.

What Google AI Pro would cost you otherwise

Google's India plans page lists Google AI Pro at ₹1,950 a month with 5 TB of storage, according to Google One (checked 14 October 2026). The cheaper paid storage plans are Lite at ₹59 a month for 30 GB and Basic at ₹130 for 100 GB. Neither includes the Gemini AI features.

Between those two sits Google AI Plus, which launched in India in December 2025 at ₹399 a month after an introductory ₹199 a month for six months, TechCrunch reported. AI Plus includes 200 GB of storage, higher Gemini limits and can be shared with up to five family members. When your free 18 months run out, decide whether you need the full AI Pro or whether AI Plus, or Basic storage on its own, covers what you actually use.

Airtel's Perplexity Pro offer has ended for new users

Airtel's app FAQ says the Perplexity Pro offer ran from 17 July 2025 to 16 January 2026 and has now expired, according to Airtel. Perplexity's own help centre confirms the promotion ended on 16 January 2026, according to Perplexity. TelecomTalk reported in February 2026 that new customers can no longer claim it.

People who did claim it keep 12 months of Pro from the date they activated it, but there are conditions. Airtel says access continues only if you have updated your payment details with Perplexity. Perplexity's help page says a credit card was needed to redeem the offer, with no charge during the free period. Anyone already paying through the Apple or Google app stores had to turn off auto-renewal, otherwise they would keep being charged. Because claims ran until January 2026, the earliest free years ended in July 2026 and the last will end in January 2027. Check your Perplexity account settings now so you are not charged without noticing.

What Airtel offers now

Airtel's current offer is smaller and is about storage, not an AI assistant. Its FAQ lists six months of Google One with 100 GB of storage at no extra cost for postpaid and Wi-Fi customers on selected plans. The postpaid plans are ₹499, ₹749, ₹1,049, ₹1,249, ₹1,449 and ₹1,799. After the trial, ₹125 a month is added to your bill from month seven, and you agree to that "Add to Bill" charge when you claim. Airtel's page does not mention Gemini, so treat this as a storage deal rather than an AI plan.

ChatGPT Go: OpenAI's free year and what comes after

When ChatGPT Go launched in August 2025, OpenAI said it gave ten times the free tier's limits on messages, image generation and file uploads, plus longer memory, and that it could be paid for through UPI, according to TechCrunch. At ₹399 a month it costs a fifth of ChatGPT Plus, which was ₹1,999 a month at the time.

The free year was offered to Indian users who signed up during a limited promotion starting 4 November 2025, and existing Go subscribers in India were also eligible, TechCrunch reported. OpenAI did not say how long sign-ups would stay open. We could not confirm from OpenAI's own pages whether new users can still claim it: the official help and pricing pages blocked our automated fetch. So open ChatGPT's subscription settings and check your own account. The first free years started in November 2025, so the earliest renewals fall from November 2026. Look up your renewal date there and decide before then whether you want to keep paying ₹399 a month.

One change since the launch is worth knowing. In January 2026 OpenAI said it would start testing ads for adult users of the free and Go tiers in the United States, SiliconANGLE reported. OpenAI pledged not to share conversations with advertisers. The report did not mention India, but the free and Go tiers are the ones OpenAI chose for the ad test, while Plus and higher plans were left out.

Privacy: what you agree to with a free AI plan

None of these deals changes how the AI company handles your data. You accept the same terms as a paying user, and the default settings are not the most private ones.

Take Gemini. Google's privacy help page, updated on 13 October 2026, says that with Keep Activity switched on, your chats help Google improve its services, including training its generative AI models, according to Google. A sample of chats is read by human reviewers, and Google keeps reviewed chats for up to three years even if you delete your activity. Activity is deleted automatically after 18 months by default, and you can change that to 3 or 36 months. If you switch Keep Activity off, or use a temporary chat, Google keeps the conversation for 72 hours and does not use it for training.

Perplexity's privacy notice, last updated on 8 July 2026, says it uses data to improve or create its services, "including our AI models", according to Perplexity. It points to an Incognito mode that does not save your search history between sessions.

Some simple habits help. Do not paste Aadhaar numbers, bank statements, medical reports or a client's confidential files into a free consumer chatbot. Use temporary or incognito chats for anything sensitive. If you sign in with a work Google account, check whether your employer allows it.

Which free AI plan suits which user

Students and heavy Google users

If you already use Gmail, Google Docs and Google Photos, Jio's AI Pro offer is the most valuable of the three. The storage alone covers years of phone photos, and NotebookLM and Deep Research are useful for coursework and research. The catch is that you must stay on a qualifying 5G plan. If you were going to recharge for ₹349 or more anyway, the AI plan costs you nothing extra.

People who mainly want answers with sources

Perplexity's strength is search-style answers with links to where each fact came from. If you claimed the Airtel offer, compare what you use it for against the free tiers before your year ends.

Writers, job seekers and small teams

ChatGPT Go is the cheapest paid ChatGPT tier, at ₹399 a month. Like Google AI Plus at the same price, it is a sensible tier to drop down to once a free year ends. Job seekers can use either to tailor CVs and practise interviews. If you are hunting for roles in this field, our AI and ML jobs board lists openings from official careers pages.

For a broader view of which assistant suits which kind of work, see our guide to the best AI tools for startups. Our free tools page has salary calculators to help you weigh any subscription against your take-home pay.

Bottom line

If you are on Jio and already pay ₹349 or more for 5G, claim the Google AI Pro offer: it is the most generous deal on the market. Jio's corporate-plan page says nothing renews automatically after 18 months, but check the terms shown in MyJio before you claim. If you claimed Airtel's Perplexity Pro or a free ChatGPT Go year, the deadline that matters now is your renewal date. Note it, check which payment method is on file, and decide whether the ₹399-a-month tiers from OpenAI or Google cover what you need. Whichever you keep, take two minutes to check the privacy settings, because a free plan comes with the same default data terms as a paid one. For more AI news from India, follow our news section.

FAQ

Is Jio's free Gemini Pro offer still available?

Yes. Jio's offer page lists it for users aged 18 and over on an active 5G plan of ₹349 or more, claimed through the MyJio app. Jio gives no end date, so check the app first.

Can I still get Perplexity Pro free with Airtel?

No. Airtel and Perplexity both say the offer ended on 16 January 2026. People who claimed it before then keep 12 months of access, as long as they have a payment method on file with Perplexity.

How much does ChatGPT Go cost in India after the free year?

ChatGPT Go was ₹399 a month when it launched in India in August 2025. Check the renewal date and price in your ChatGPT subscription settings.

Will I be charged when the Jio Gemini offer ends?

Jio's business offer page says there is no payment or auto-renewal after the 18 months. After that, you can buy a Google One or AI plan yourself if you want to keep the features.

Does Google use my Gemini chats for training?

It can, if Keep Activity is on. Google says some chats are reviewed by humans and that temporary chats are not used for training. You can switch Keep Activity off from Gemini Apps Activity.
